Definition: from the same as G5494; to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale:--be tossed with tempest.
BiblicalUsage: To be tossed with tempest is the word for the ship on the way to Rome, exceedingly tossed, so that the next day they lighten the ship. The storm does the tossing and the sailors can only throw cargo overboard.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the tossing is the storm, not the end: the ship is lightened and Paul is kept, and God brings them all safe to land.
